$schema_note: P1 () shared vector fixture. Pins the cross-chain DEX fill-quantization contract between the hub's CrossChainDexEngine bottleneck clamp and the indexer's actions/order_match.js. Both repos vendor this file BYTE-IDENTICALLY and each side's unit suite asserts its own half, so neither can drift alone. A diff here is a consensus-visible change to fill quantities and must be reviewed as one.
authority: Canonical copy lives in xchain-hub/test/fixtures/; vendored byte-identical into xchain-indexer/test/fixtures/. Regenerating means re-deriving BOTH halves and re-reviewing, not copying one side's output over the other.
contract: 1. The derived side of the bottleneck clamp is multiplied at PRECISION 64 on both sides. The hub ran this at 18 (fixed 2026-07-28); getPrice already yields a 64-digit rate, so 18 discarded digits the indexer keeps.
2. bcround is floor(n * 10^d + 0.5) / 10^d, half-up, explicit and config-independent, identical in xchain-indexer/src/utility.js and xchain-hub/src/bcmath.js.

3. TICK QUANTIZATION IS NOT YET AT PARITY. The indexer snaps both derived amounts onto their own tick's decimal grid (order_match.js:219-220). The hub cannot: its cross-chain offers carry give_tick/get_tick but no decimals, and it mirrors no token table. The `tick_quantization` vectors below therefore pin the INDEXER's behavior only, and are marked hub_reachable:false. They become a parity requirement the moment offers carry decimals.

precision_alignment.label: recurring price, get-side bottleneck
precision_alignment.note: 1/3 is not finitely representable, so precision 18 vs 64 diverge in the digits the indexer retains. This is the vector that made the two engines derive different fills.

precision_alignment.label: last-satoshi fill, exact price
precision_alignment.note: An exactly representable price agrees at both precisions. Included so the fixture proves the 18-vs-64 change is NOT a blanket behavior change: it only moves the inexact cases.

precision_alignment.label: sub-tick remainder, give-side bottleneck
precision_alignment.note: give_from_get (3.5) exceeds max_give (1), so give clamps to max_give and get is derived from the taker's ask. The clamp step is exact at both precisions; the DERIVED get is where 18 and 64 diverge, which is why this branch needs the fix too and not just the get-side branch.

tick_quantization.label: sub-ULP artifact recovers to a whole unit
tick_quantization.note: The canonical reason bcround exists: a 64-digit derivation can land one ULP under an exact integer, and the grid snap recovers it.

tick_quantization.label: indivisible (0-decimal) tick forces an integer fill
tick_quantization.note: An NFT-style tick must never settle a fractional quantity. A COIN_DECIMALS=8 default would silently pass 1.6 through here, which is why the hub must not guess decimals.

tick_quantization.label: half-up at the grid boundary
tick_quantization.note: Pins the rounding MODE, not just the width: banker's rounding would give 0.00000002.

tick_quantization.label: dust below the grid rounds to zero and the fill is dropped
tick_quantization.note: Both engines drop a fill that quantizes to zero rather than settling dust.
